summary: Fork of @whiskeysockets/baileys with import-time phone-home and unpinned personal-account dependency
details: @alannxd/baileys is a republished fork of @whiskeysockets/baileys (WhatsApp library) whose README is cloned from the upstream project. On every require()/import of the package main, lib/index.js performs an unconditional HTTPS fetch to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information.json, parses the JSON, and logs a string field to the console; no installer data is sent outbound and the response is not eval'd, written to disk, or otherwise executed. package.json also declares the runtime dependency `libsignal` as `github:@alannzxd/libsignal-node` with no commit SHA or tag pin, so npm resolves this transitive against the current HEAD of a personal-account repo at install time, leaving the actual code pulled into the dependency tree mutable and post-publish-controllable by that account. The static `ping` keyword match in lib/Utils/generics.js corresponds to inherited upstream baileys utility code, not to a network command-execution path. No exfiltration of environment variables, credentials, or filesystem contents is present in this version, no install/import-time RCE mechanism is present (the fetched JSON is not executed), and no destructive action runs at install. The combination — fork of a WhatsApp library, import-time mutable author-controlled channel, and unpinned mutable github: dependency on a related personal account — is a meaningful distribution-channel risk worth a human decision but does not currently demonstrate installer harm in this version's traced code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
